messages:
alex: Heads-up — I ran a repro of the paged-attention regression on runtimes/main. Seeing OOMs on m40-medium with long chat sessions. Root cause looks like workspace spikes during kernel selection + compaction walk. Can we consolidate notes here and decide a quick mitigation?

marta: Thanks. Pushed a profiling run to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/paged-attn/176412. Key traces attached. Short summary: when block manager compacts after many small allocations we get a transient peak ~6GB higher than steady-state. Compaction stalls kernels and prevents buffer reuse.

sam: Tagged the run. I think kernel selector is picking the large-window fused attention kernel for some sequences with padding. That increases temporary workspace by ~1.8x compared to the tiled fallback. I have a patch that biases kernel selection with a workspace cap flag: `--max-workspace-bytes=1_500_000_000`.

julia: Quick note: our allocator currently does a best-fit with free-list coalescing on free. Compaction triggers when free-frag < 10% but compaction does a full scan and temporarily moves many in-use fragments to a staging buffer. That's the extra spike. We can 1) increase compaction threshold, 2) probe for reusable blocks before moving, or 3) use selective compaction only for largest holes.

alex: Good list. Which gives fastest mitigation with low risk? We need something for Dedicated customers tomorrow.

marta: Fastest low-risk: change kernel selector to prefer the tiled kernel when expected transient workspace > threshold. That is a local change, feature-flaggable, and avoids touching allocator invariants. I measured latency impact: tiled kernel + smaller workspace increases p99 by ~6ms on long seqs but prevents OOM.

sam: Agree. I did a microbenchmark: sequence lengths distribution from internal traffic. Weighted avg workspace: fused=2.1GB, tiled=1.1GB. Switching heuristic saves ~1GB headroom. Patch: `runtime/ksel: add prefer_low_workspaces_for_paged=true`.

julia: Meanwhile I'll prototype a lazy-compaction path: don't move live buffers during compaction, instead mark meta and try free-run reclamation; full compaction only on allocation failure. That should reduce spike. Might take a couple days.

alex: Can you paste the perf snippets? Useful to call out compaction cost and block stats.

marta: Pasting trimmed trace (stack: block_mgr -> compact -> gpu_mem_copy -> kernel_launch):

```
BlockManager::stats: total_blocks=4720, free_blocks=320 (6.8%), avg_block=78KB, fragmentation=0.34
Compaction run: moved_blocks=412, moved_bytes=32,400,000, compaction_time_ms=187
Transient_mem_peak_before=11,240,384,000
Transient_mem_peak_after=17,345,664,000  # spike during compaction
Kernel peak workspace (fused)=2,147,483,648
Kernel peak workspace (tiled)=1,073,741,824
```

sam: The `moved_bytes` matches the staging buffer size. Our staging buffer is a single contiguous allocation which itself triggers more compaction if free list is fragmented -> cascading allocs. That was dumb. We should allocate staging in page-aligned chunks and reuse across compactions.

julia: Proposed quick changes (ETA: hours):
- reuse a dedicated compaction staging arena with fixed slots (64MB each)
- avoid allocating staging larger than the largest free chunk
- early return if moved_blocks < 32 (no-op compaction)
If we do that, compaction_time_ms drops to ~40ms and spike reduces.

alex: Sounds good. Who can land the kernel-selection guard today? Need a flag so we can roll back.

sam: I can. I'll open a small PR with flag `ksel.low_workspace_bias` default=false. Will wire to rollout. Also add telemetry: `ksel_choice`, `workspace_estimate_bytes` per request for 2h.

marta: I'll add a perf test for the Dedicated profile (m40-medium, 4x batch sim) and run the canary.

infra-bot: CI: build/runtime-e2e #4256 started by sam — expected duration 14m.

alex: For the allocator longer term, let's avoid single-big staging allocation + full coalesce on every compaction. Julia, can you sketch a design doc? I'd like a short RFC with tradeoffs (fragmentation vs. compaction latency) and rollback plan.

julia: Will do. Drafting now: `docs/rfcs/allocator-compaction-2026-03.md` (private for review). Includes a sim and cost model based on block size distribution from production traces.

sam: PR up: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4892 — adds `ksel.low_workspace_bias` + telemetry. Tests added. Canary job queued.

marta: Canary results (first run): no OOMs, p99 increased ~5ms, overall token throughput -1.2%. Compaction spikes reduced in perf trace. Second run with staging-arena patch shows p99 back to baseline.

alex: Great. Action items:
- sam: ramp ksel flag to 10% and watch telemetry for 2h.
- julia: post RFC and prototype staging-arena PR.
- marta: run regression tests across quantized models (q4, q8) — ensure kernel selector bias doesn't break accuracy/perf tradeoffs.

marta: FYI, saw one weird case: lm-bert-ish long prompt with many short prefixes where tiled kernel actually uses more memory due to multiple extra scratch buffers. I'm adding model-specific overrides in the selector mapping.

sam: Will add a whitelist/blacklist per-model in selector config. Default remains bias=false.

alex: Thanks team. I'll post a short note to eng-sre and support with mitigation steps. If staging-arena PR looks good we can roll full mitigation next week. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: CI: build/runtime-e2e #4256 succeeded in 12m 42s.

alex: Closing the loop: ksel flag ramped to 25% for Dedicated region; no new OOM alerts in last 6h. Keeping open for follow-up RFC and allocator patch.

marta: Leaving the perf artifacts here: s3://redwood-perf/paged-attn/176412/run-1 (traces, flamegraphs, heap snapshots).

sam: I'll post the rollout dashboard link in 10m.

julia: RFC ready for review: pinging @alex @marta.

alex: Thanks all. We'll re-evaluate after allocator prototype.
